items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1973-09-07
items.q: Yeah, yeah, Dutre taught me, Roy taught me more so.

ctx.x: Dutre taught you how to read?

Yeah, yeah, Dutre taught me, Roy taught me more so. And then I, later on as I progressed, I joined Eli Rice's band. I stayed with him about 14 months. We traveled all through Wisconsin and Minnesota and Michigan, Michigan and Minnesota. And I used to get out there in them woods and practice. So after 14 months I came back to Chicago and I played the great pianist Teddy Weller for him at the Dream. And Shirley Clare was on the cornet myself and Teddy and I had forgotten the fellow who could play drum and sing very…
I think Audis Starks was on there, Clamondon and Saxe.

items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: And I'd be getting different pointers from Dutre. I used to sit, I sat behind Dutre about four or five consecutive years.

ctx.x: So when was the first music that you were interested in? Did you start on the trombone or which instrument did you start on?

Well, my first instrument was trombone, but it wasn't my favorite instrument. I'd like to tell you, Bill, about how I come to study the trombone. While talking with Joe Oliver, it must have been somewhere around 1920, 1921, somewhere along there. He, I told Joe Oliver that I was going to take lessons on the trombone. So he says, why don't you try the clarinet? The reason Joe suggested to me to take the, take up the clarinet was because I used to whistle so good. And he said people did. So he thought if a fella…
